signature.name: Window of the World
signature.detail: Shenzhen's most famous attraction, a theme park packed with miniature replicas of world landmarks from the Eiffel Tower to the Pyramids. It is a classic first-timer stop and great for families. Go on a weekday morning to avoid crowds, and bring water since the park is large and sunny.

signature.name: Ping An International Finance Centre
signature.detail: One of the tallest skyscrapers in China and the defining tower of Shenzhen's skyline. The observation deck gives sweeping views over the city and toward Hong Kong on clear days. Visit near sunset for the best light, and book tickets online in advance.

signature.name: Lianhuashan Park
signature.detail: A large hilltop park with lawns, a famous statue and panoramic views of the Futian skyline. It is a favorite spot for locals and a relaxed break from the city. Come in the late afternoon for cooler weather and skyline photos.

signature.name: Shenzhen Museum
signature.detail: The best place to understand Shenzhen's rapid rise from fishing village to megacity. Exhibits cover local history and culture, and entry is typically free. It is a good rainy-day or midday option; check opening hours before you go.

signature.name: OCT-LOFT Creative Culture Park
signature.detail: A converted factory district full of galleries, design shops and cafes, and the heart of Shenzhen's creative scene. It is ideal for a relaxed afternoon of browsing and photos. Go on a weekday for a quieter visit.

signature.name: Splendid China Folk Village
signature.detail: A large cultural theme park with miniature versions of famous Chinese sites and performances of ethnic minority culture. It suits visitors who want a compact overview of China's landmarks and traditions. Plan a half day and check show times on arrival.
